intent: Compare the market adoption trajectories over time across the aggressive replacement scenarios and the market-driven and carbon-tax scenarios to determine how each scenario's adoption level evolves.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
How do the aggressive replacement scenarios' adoption trajectories evolve over time?
How do the market-driven and carbon-tax scenarios' adoption trajectories evolve over time?
How do the adoption levels compare across the aggressive replacement scenarios and the market-driven and carbon-tax scenarios over time?

units.claim: All 7 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: In the single panel, the aggressive replacement scenarios (Early retirement of worst emitters, 100% replacement at end of life, Production ramp then 100% replacement) all rise from 0% adoption at point_order 1 to 100% adoption by their final shown point_order (4, 3, and 3 respectively), with Early retirement reaching 35% at point_order 2 before hitting 100% at point_order 3.
units.computation: For each aggressive replacement series, verify the start value at point_order 1 is 0%, the end value at the final point_order is 100%, and for Early retirement verify the intermediate value 35% at point_order 2.
accept: All three aggressive replacement series start at 0% at point_order 1.
All three aggressive replacement series reach 100% by their final shown point_order.
Early retirement of worst emitters shows 35% at point_order 2 before reaching 100% at point_order 3.
reject: Any aggressive replacement series does not start at 0%.
Any aggressive replacement series does not reach 100%.
Early retirement of worst emitters does not show 35% at point_order 2.

units.claim: In the single panel, the market-driven and carbon-tax scenarios (High carbon tax, Low market subsidy, Low carbon tax, Free market) all rise monotonically from 0% at point_order 1 to their respective final values at point_order 61: High carbon tax 82%, Low market subsidy 72%, Low carbon tax 60%, and Free market 55%.
units.computation: For each of the four market-driven and carbon-tax series, verify the value at point_order 1 is 0% and the value at point_order 61 is as stated (82, 72, 60, 55). Monotonic increase is supported by the full row set but the minimal proof uses endpoints.
accept: High carbon tax ends at 82% at point_order 61.
Low market subsidy ends at 72% at point_order 61.
Low carbon tax ends at 60% at point_order 61.
Free market ends at 55% at point_order 61.
All four series start at 0% at point_order 1.
reject: Any series does not start at 0%.
Any final value differs from the stated value.
The series are not shown as increasing over time.

units.claim: In the single panel, the aggressive replacement scenarios reach 100% adoption much earlier (by point_order 3 or 4) than the market-driven and carbon-tax scenarios, which by point_order 61 reach only 55% to 82%; among the market-driven and carbon-tax scenarios at point_order 61, High carbon tax is highest (82%), followed by Low market subsidy (72%), Low carbon tax (60%), and Free market (55%).
units.computation: Compare the point_order at which each aggressive replacement series reaches 100% (3, 2, 2) with the final values of the market-driven and carbon-tax series at point_order 61 (82, 72, 60, 55). Also order the four market-driven and carbon-tax final values descending.
accept: Aggressive replacement scenarios reach 100% by point_order 3 or earlier.
Market-driven and carbon-tax scenarios are still below 100% at point_order 61, with final values between 55% and 82%.
At point_order 61, High carbon tax > Low market subsidy > Low carbon tax > Free market.
reject: Any aggressive replacement scenario does not reach 100% by point_order 4.
Any market-driven or carbon-tax scenario reaches 100% by point_order 61.
The ordering of final values among market-driven and carbon-tax scenarios is incorrect.

optional_valid: Mention that Early retirement of worst emitters has an intermediate value of 35% at point_order 2.
Mention that the market-driven and carbon-tax series have 61 points while aggressive replacement series have 3 or 4 points.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for why scenarios differ.
Exact values at intermediate point_orders for market-driven and carbon-tax scenarios beyond the endpoints.
Claims about crossing points between series.
Claims about percentage change or ratios between scenarios.
review_notes: The intent asks to compare trajectories across two groups of scenarios and determine how each scenario's adoption level evolves. Three semantic units cover: (1) aggressive replacement trends, (2) market-driven and carbon-tax trends, and (3) cross-group comparison of adoption levels over time.
The x-axis is time but x values are empty; point_order is used as the time proxy.

The aggressive replacement series have different numbers of points (4, 3, 3) and reach 100% at different point_orders; the comparison unit captures that they reach 100% much earlier than the other group.
No crossing or threshold units are needed because the intent does not explicitly ask for them and the data does not show crossings among the main series.
